```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.asp = 0.6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
```

# Problem 1

## Import and inspect the data

```{r import_noaa}
data("ny_noaa")

dim(ny_noaa)
glimpse(ny_noaa)
```

The original dataset contains 2,595,176 daily weather records from 747 stations in New York State, covering 1981–2010. Each row represents one station on one date. Variables include precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and daily maximum and minimum temperatures. Missingness varies across variables: approximately 5.6% for precipitation, 14.7% for snowfall, 22.8% for snow depth, and 43.7% for each temperature variable.

I extracted year, month, and day from the date. I converted the temperature variables from character to numeric and expressed temperatures in degrees Celsius and precipitation in millimeters. Snowfall and snow depth were already recorded in millimeters.

```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    n_stations = n_distinct(id),
    first_date = min(date),
    last_date = max(date)
  )

ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    prcp_missing_pct = mean(is.na(prcp)) * 100,
    snow_missing_pct = mean(is.na(snow)) * 100,
    snwd_missing_pct = mean(is.na(snwd)) * 100,
    tmax_missing_pct = mean(is.na(tmax)) * 100,
    tmin_missing_pct = mean(is.na(tmin)) * 100
  )
```

```{r}
noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

dim(noaa_df)
glimpse(noaa_df)
```

```{r}
noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Number of observations")
  )
```

Zero is the most common snowfall value, reflecting the many station-days without snowfall. Common positive values include 25, 13, 51, and 76 mm. These values are close to common inch increments, suggesting that unit conversion and rounding may contribute to the observed pattern.

```{r}
monthly_temp_df =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(
    month %in% c(1, 7),
    !is.na(tmax)
  ) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax),
    n_days = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

head(monthly_temp_df)
```

```{r}
monthly_temp_df |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = mean_tmax,
      group = id
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average maximum temperature by station and year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean daily maximum temperature (°C)",
    caption = "Monthly means use available daily temperature records."
  )
```

Average maximum temperatures are much higher in July than in January. Temperatures vary across stations, and many stations show similar year-to-year changes. January shows larger year-to-year fluctuations. Station USC00308962 has an unusually low mean maximum temperature of about 14.0°C in July 1988. This mean is based on 31 daily records, so it is not explained by a small number of observed days. The underlying measurements should be checked before interpreting this value.

```{r}
temp_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(
    !is.na(tmin),
    !is.na(tmax)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 50) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    trans = "log10",
    name = "Count"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily minimum and maximum temperatures",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)"
  )
```

```{r}
snow_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(
    snow > 0,
    snow < 100
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_violin(
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = as.character(seq(1985, 2010, by = 5))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of positive snowfall below 100 mm",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  )
```

```{r combined_noaa_plots, fig.width=8, fig.asp=1}
temp_plot / snow_plot
```

Daily minimum and maximum temperatures show a strong positive association: days with higher minimum temperatures generally also have higher maximum temperatures. The two-dimensional bin plot shows where observations are concentrated without excessive overlap. A few isolated extreme values may indicate data quality issues and should be checked.
Among records with snowfall greater than 0 and less than 100 mm, smaller snowfall amounts are more common. The distributions have similar shapes across years, with concentrations near 25, 50, and 75 mm. There is no obvious consistent shift over time in these selected snowfall distributions. This plot does not compare annual snowfall totals.

# Problem 2

## Data cleaning and merging

```{r clean_nhanes_covar}
nhanes_covar =
  read_csv(
    "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
    skip = 4,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
  rename(
    seqn = SEQN,
    bmi = BMI
  ) |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na(sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  mutate(
    seqn = as.character(seqn),
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )

dim(nhanes_covar)
```

```{r tidy_merge_nhanes}
nhanes_accel_long =
  read_csv(
    "data/nhanes_accel.csv",
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
  rename(seqn = SEQN) |>
  mutate(seqn = as.character(seqn)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims"
  ) |>
  mutate(minute = as.integer(minute))

nhanes_df =
  nhanes_covar |>
  left_join(nhanes_accel_long, by = "seqn")

dim(nhanes_df)

nhanes_df |>
  summarize(
    n_participants = n_distinct(seqn),
    missing_mims = sum(is.na(mims))
  )
```

After excluding participants younger than 21 years and those with missing demographic information, 228 participants remain. The merged dataset contains 328,320 participant-minute observations, with 1,440 minutes per participant and no missing MIMS values among retained participants.

## Participants by education and sex

```{r nhanes_education_table}
nhanes_covar |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Education level", "Male", "Female")
  )
```

## Age distributions

```{r nhanes_age_plot, fig.width=9, fig.asp=0.45}
nhanes_covar |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Male" = "#0072B2", "Female" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Age distributions by sex and education",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The largest education category is more than high school, with 115 participants. Numbers of men and women are similar in the lowest and highest education categories, whereas the high school equivalent group includes more men than women (35 versus 23).

Participants with more than high school education have lower median ages: 43.5 years for men and 41 years for women. In the high school equivalent group, women have a higher median age than men (62 versus 53 years). Median ages are similar for men and women with less than high school education (60 and 61 years).

## Total daily activity and age

```{r nhanes_total_activity, fig.width=9, fig.asp=0.5}
nhanes_total =
  nhanes_df |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  summarize(
    total_activity = sum(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

nhanes_total |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Male" = "#0072B2", "Female" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity and age",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total daily activity (sum of MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Total daily activity tends to decrease with age for both men and women within each education category. There is substantial individual variability and overlap between the sexes. The fitted trends differ across education groups, but these descriptive associations do not establish causal effects of age, sex, or education on activity.

## Activity patterns over 24 hours

```{r nhanes_daily_patterns, fig.width=9, fig.asp=0.5}
nhanes_time =
  nhanes_df |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute) |>
  summarize(
    mean_mims = mean(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hour = (minute - 1) / 60
  )

nhanes_time |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = mean_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    span = 0.2,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Male" = "#0072B2", "Female" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average activity over 24 hours",
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = "Mean minute-level activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Across all education groups, average activity is lowest overnight, increases in the morning, remains elevated during the day, and declines in the late evening. Among participants with more than high school education, women generally have higher daytime activity than men. Sex differences are smaller and vary over the day in the other education groups. These group averages are not adjusted for differences in age or other characteristics.

# Problem 3

## Import and clean the data

```{r import_citibike}
citibike_df =
  bind_rows(
    read_csv(
      "data/citibike/Jan 2020 Citi.csv",
      show_col_types = FALSE
    ) |> mutate(year = 2020, month = "January"),

    read_csv(
      "data/citibike/July 2020 Citi.csv",
      show_col_types = FALSE
    ) |> mutate(year = 2020, month = "July"),

    read_csv(
      "data/citibike/Jan 2024 Citi.csv",
      show_col_types = FALSE
    ) |> mutate(year = 2024, month = "January"),

    read_csv(
      "data/citibike/July 2024 Citi.csv",
      show_col_types = FALSE
    ) |> mutate(year = 2024, month = "July")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July")),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c(
        "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
        "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
      )
    ),
    member_casual = factor(
      member_casual,
      levels = c("casual", "member"),
      labels = c("Casual", "Member")
    ),
    rideable_type = factor(
      rideable_type,
      levels = c("classic_bike", "electric_bike"),
      labels = c("Classic", "Electric")
    )
  )

dim(citibike_df)

citibike_df |>
  summarize(
    missing_start_station = sum(is.na(start_station_name)),
    missing_end_station = sum(is.na(end_station_name)),
    missing_duration = sum(is.na(duration))
  )
```

The combined dataset contains 99,485 rides and nine variables, covering January and July of 2020 and 2024. Each row represents one ride, with information on ride ID, bicycle type, day of the week, duration in minutes, starting and ending stations, and membership status. Year and month identify the source file. The supplied data are 1% samples of rides lasting less than four hours in each month.

There are 43 missing starting-station names and 207 missing ending-station names, but no missing ride durations. These records are retained for analyses that do not require station names.

## Ride counts by year, month, and membership

```{r citibike_counts}
citibike_df |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(Total = Casual + Member) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Casual", "Member", "Total"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )
```

Members account for most rides in every year-month combination. July has more sampled rides than January in both years, and the corresponding months have more rides in 2024 than in 2020. July 2024 has the largest total, with 47,156 rides. These counts describe the supplied samples rather than all Citi Bike rides.

## Most popular starting stations in July 2024

```{r citibike_top_stations}
citibike_df |>
  filter(year == "2024", month == "July") |>
  drop_na(start_station_name) |>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Starting station", "Number of rides")
  )
```

## Median ride duration by day of the week

```{r citibike_weekday_plot, fig.width=9, fig.asp=0.5}
citibike_median =
  citibike_df |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

citibike_median |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = weekdays,
      y = median_duration,
      color = month,
      group = month
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("January" = "#0072B2", "July" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median ride duration by weekday, month, and year",
    x = "Day of the week",
    y = "Median ride duration (minutes)",
    color = "Month"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Median ride durations are higher in July than in January in both years, and higher in 2020 than in 2024 for the corresponding month and weekday. The weekend increase is particularly pronounced in July 2020, when median durations are approximately 16.5 minutes on Saturday and Sunday, compared with roughly 13–14 minutes on weekdays. January 2024 shows a much weaker weekend pattern.

## Ride duration distributions in 2024

```{r citibike_2024_distribution, fig.width=8, fig.asp=0.7}
citibike_df |>
  filter(year == "2024") |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = rideable_type,
      y = duration,
      fill = rideable_type
    )
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.6,
    outlier.alpha = 0.15,
    outlier.size = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_grid(month ~ member_casual) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Classic" = "#0072B2", "Electric" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 60)) +
  labs(
    title = "Ride duration distributions in 2024",
    x = "Bicycle type",
    y = "Ride duration (minutes)",
    caption = "Display limited to 60 minutes; longer rides remain in boxplot calculations."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Ride-duration distributions are right-skewed, with some unusually long rides. Casual riders generally have longer median durations than members, and July medians exceed January medians within each membership and bicycle-type combination. Among casual riders, classic-bike trips have higher median durations than electric-bike trips. Among members, electric-bike medians are slightly higher than classic-bike medians, particularly in July. The figure displays durations up to 60 minutes, while retaining longer rides in the boxplot calculations.
